units.zh: 姚泓
units.en: Yao Hong.
units.literal: Section heading: Yao Hong.

units.zh: 姚泓，字元子，興之長子也。
units.en: Yao Hong, courtesy Yuanzi, was Yao Xing's firstborn.
units.literal: Yao Hong, courtesy name Yuanzi, was the eldest son of Yao Xing.

proposals.before: Yao Hong, courtesy Yuanzi, was Yao Xing's firstborn.
proposals.after: Yao Hong, whose courtesy name was Yuanzi, was Yao Xing’s eldest son.
proposals.reason: 長子 identifies the eldest son. “Firstborn” omits that he is a son and could imply that he is the eldest of all the children.

units.zh: 孝友寬和，而無經世之用，又多疾病，興將以為嗣而疑焉。
units.en: He was dutiful, gentle, and kind, but had no talent for governing a realm, and he was often ill—so Yao Xing long hesitated before naming him heir.
units.literal: He was filial, friendly, generous, and mild, yet lacked the ability to order the age, and moreover often fell ill; Xing was about to make him heir yet hesitated.

proposals.before: He was dutiful, gentle, and kind, but had no talent for governing a realm, and he was often ill—so Yao Xing long hesitated before naming him heir.
proposals.after: He was dutiful to his parents, affectionate toward his brothers, generous and mild. But he lacked the ability to govern and was often ill, so Yao Xing hesitated over making him heir.
proposals.reason: 孝友 includes devotion to siblings as well as filial piety.

proposals.before: He was filial, friendly, generous, and mild, yet lacked the ability to order the age, and moreover often fell ill; Xing was about to make him heir yet hesitated.
proposals.after: He was filial, affectionate toward his brothers, generous and mild, yet lacked the ability to govern the realm and was often ill. Xing intended to make him heir but hesitated.
proposals.reason: 友 in 孝友 denotes affection toward siblings.

value.statement: filial, friendly, generous, and mild, but lacking talent for governing

units.zh: 久之，乃立為太子。
units.en: At length Yao Xing named him crown prince.
units.literal: After a long time, he was then established as heir apparent.

units.zh: 興每征伐巡遊，常留總後事。
units.en: Whenever Yao Xing marched or toured, he left Yao Hong in charge of the rear.
units.literal: Whenever Xing on campaign or inspection tour, he regularly left him behind to oversee rear affairs.

value.action: left in charge during campaigns and tours of p002

units.zh: 博學善談論，尤好詩詠。
units.en: He was learned, a fluent talker, and especially loved poetry.
units.literal: He was broadly learned and good at discourse, especially fond of poetry and recitation.

units.zh: 尚書王尚、黃門郎段章、尚書郎富允文以儒術侍講，胡義周、夏侯稚以文章遊集。
units.en: Wang Shang, Duan Zhang, and Fu Yunwen tutored him in the classics; Hu Yizhou and Xiahou Zhi kept him company over belles-lettres.
units.literal: Director Wang Shang, Gentleman of the Yellow Gates Duan Zhang, and Director Gentleman Fu Yunwen attended lectures with Confucian learning; Hu Yizhou and Xiahou Zhi gathered in literary companionship.

proposals.before: Wang Shang, Duan Zhang, and Fu Yunwen tutored him in the classics; Hu Yizhou and Xiahou Zhi kept him company over belles-lettres.
proposals.after: Wang Shang, a master of writing, Duan Zhang, a gentleman of the Yellow Gates, and Fu Yunwen, a gentleman of the Department of State Affairs, tutored him in the classics. Hu Yizhou and Xiahou Zhi joined him for literary gatherings.
proposals.reason: Restore the distinct offices of all three Confucian tutors.

proposals.before: Director Wang Shang, Gentleman of the Yellow Gates Duan Zhang, and Director Gentleman Fu Yunwen attended lectures with Confucian learning; Hu Yizhou and Xiahou Zhi gathered in literary companionship.
proposals.after: Master of Writing Wang Shang, Gentleman of the Yellow Gates Duan Zhang, and gentleman of the Department of State Affairs Fu Yunwen attended him as lecturers on Confucian learning. Hu Yizhou and Xiahou Zhi joined him in literary gatherings.
proposals.reason: 侍講 describes lecturing to Hong, not attending lectures as pupils; 尚書郎 is a departmental gentleman.

units.zh: 時尚書王敏、右丞郭播以刑政過寬，議欲峻制，泓曰：「人情挫辱，則壯厲之心生；
units.en: Director Wang Min and aide Guo Bo thought the laws too soft and pressed for crackdowns. Yao Hong replied: "Humiliate people and you breed defiance.
units.literal: At the time Director Wang Min and right aide Guo Bo, because punishments and government were too lenient, debated wishing for harsh regulation. Hong said, "When human feelings are humiliated, a fierce and stern mind arises;

proposals.before: Director Wang Min and aide Guo Bo thought the laws too soft and pressed for crackdowns. Yao Hong replied: "Humiliate people and you breed defiance.
proposals.after: Wang Min, a master of writing, and Guo Bo, the right assistant director, thought the administration of punishments too lenient and proposed stricter regulations. Yao Hong replied, “Humiliate people and you breed defiance.
proposals.reason: 右丞 specifies Guo’s office and 以刑政過寬 covers punishments and governance.

units.zh: 政教煩苛，則苟免之行立。
units.en: Smother them in petty rules and they learn only to dodge.
units.literal: When government and instruction are fussy and harsh, conduct of bare escape is established.

units.zh: 上之化下，如風靡草。
units.en: Those above shape those below as wind bends grass.
units.literal: What is above transforms what is below, like wind bending grass.

units.zh: 君等參贊朝化，弘昭政軌，不務仁恕之道，惟欲嚴法酷刑，豈是安上馭下之理乎！」
units.en: You help run the court—widen the path of mercy, not the jailer's whip; harshness is no way to steady ruler and people."
units.literal: You gentlemen assist and join in court transformation, broadly display the tracks of government—if you do not pursue the way of benevolence and forgiveness, but only desire harsh laws and cruel punishments, how could that be the principle of quieting those above and controlling those below!"

proposals.before: You help run the court—widen the path of mercy, not the jailer's whip; harshness is no way to steady ruler and people."
proposals.after: You gentlemen help guide the court and make its principles of government known. If you neglect humanity and clemency and seek only strict laws and cruel punishments, how can you keep the ruler secure and govern his subjects?”
proposals.reason: The officials’ responsibility for exemplifying government policy and Hong’s rhetorical question about ruling above and below have been compressed away.

units.zh: 敏等遂止。
units.en: Wang Min and his allies dropped the idea.
units.literal: Min and others then desisted.

units.zh: 泓受經于博士淳于岐。
units.en: Yao Hong studied the classics under the erudite Chunyu Qi.
units.literal: Hong received the classics from Erudite Chunyu Qi.

units.zh: 岐病，泓親詣省疾，拜於床下。
units.en: When Chunyu Qi fell ill, Yao Hong visited his bedside and bowed on the floor.
units.literal: When Qi was ill, Hong personally went to inquire after his illness and bowed below the couch.

value.action: visited p010 in illness and bowed below the couch

units.zh: 自是公侯見師傅皆拜焉。
units.en: After that, every prince who met a tutor bowed as he had done.
units.literal: From this dukes and marquises seeing tutors all bowed.

proposals.before: After that, every prince who met a tutor bowed as he had done.
proposals.after: After that, dukes and marquises all bowed when they met their tutors.
proposals.reason: 公侯 identifies dukes and marquises.

value.action: established the practice that dukes and marquises bow to tutors

units.zh: 興之如平涼也，馮翊人劉厥聚眾數千，據萬年以叛。
units.en: When Yao Xing marched to Pingliang, Liu Jue of Fengyi raised several thousand men, seized Wannian, and rebelled.
units.literal: When Xing went to Pingliang, a man of Fengyi, Liu Jue, gathered several thousand followers, occupied Wannian, and rebelled.

value.action: gathered several thousand, occupied Wannian, rebelled

units.zh: 泓遣鎮軍彭白狼率東宮禁兵討之，斬厥，赦其餘黨。
units.en: Yao Hong sent Peng Bailang with palace guards from the heir's residence; Liu Jue was executed and the rest pardoned.
units.literal: Hong sent General Who Guards the Army Peng Bailang to lead eastern-palace household troops to campaign against him, beheaded Jue, and pardoned the rest of the faction.

proposals.before: Yao Hong sent Peng Bailang with palace guards from the heir's residence; Liu Jue was executed and the rest pardoned.
proposals.after: Yao Hong sent Peng Bailang, the General Who Guards the Army, to lead the Eastern Palace guards against Liu Jue. Jue was beheaded and the remaining rebels pardoned.
proposals.reason: Restore Peng’s military title and his commission to attack Jue.

value.action: sent p012 with eastern-palace troops against p011

units.zh: 諸將咸勸泓曰：「殿下神算電發，蕩平醜逆，宜露布表言，廣其首級，以慰遠近之情。」
units.en: His generals said: "Your victory was swift—publish a victory notice and show the heads to steady the realm."
units.literal: The generals all urged Hong, saying, "Your Highness's divine calculations strike like lightning; you have swept away the vile rebels—it is fitting to issue a public bulletin reporting it, broadly display their heads, to comfort feeling far and near."

proposals.before: His generals said: "Your victory was swift—publish a victory notice and show the heads to steady the realm."
proposals.after: All the generals urged Hong, “Your Highness devised your plans with lightning speed and swept away the vile rebels. You should issue an open dispatch reporting the victory and claiming a greater number of enemy heads, to reassure people far and near.”
proposals.reason: 廣其首級 concerns the number of heads claimed in the report. Only Jue had been beheaded in the preceding unit. The generals also praise Hong’s swift planning.

proposals.before: The generals all urged Hong, saying, "Your Highness's divine calculations strike like lightning; you have swept away the vile rebels—it is fitting to issue a public bulletin reporting it, broadly display their heads, to comfort feeling far and near."
proposals.after: All the generals urged Hong, “Your Highness devised your plans with lightning speed and swept away the vile rebels. You should issue an open dispatch reporting the victory and claiming a greater number of enemy heads, to reassure people far and near.”
proposals.reason: 廣其首級 concerns the number of heads claimed in the report. Only Jue had been beheaded in the preceding unit. The generals also praise Hong’s swift planning.

units.zh: 泓曰：「主上委吾後事，使式遏寇逆。
units.en: Yao Hong answered: "My father left me the rear to stop traitors.
units.literal: Hong said, "The lord above entrusted me with rear affairs, making me check invading rebels.

units.zh: 吾綏禦失和，以長奸寇，方當引咎責躬，歸罪行間，安敢過自矜誕，以重罪責乎！」
units.en: I mishandled the pacification and fed rebellion—I should blame myself, not strut and deepen my fault."
units.literal: I failed in pacification and control, thereby growing traitorous bandits; I ought to take blame on myself and assign guilt among the ranks—how dare I overmuch boast and swagger, thereby adding to the burden of fault!"

proposals.before: I mishandled the pacification and fed rebellion—I should blame myself, not strut and deepen my fault."
proposals.after: I failed to strike the right balance in pacifying and defending the people, and so encouraged the rebels. I ought now to take the blame, reproach myself and acknowledge my guilt before the ranks. How dare I boast extravagantly and make my fault still greater?”
proposals.reason: The sentence connects failures of pacification and defense to the rise of rebellion and adds 歸罪行間 after Hong takes personal responsibility. Preserve the military setting without shifting the blame onto his subordinates.

proposals.before: I failed in pacification and control, thereby growing traitorous bandits; I ought to take blame on myself and assign guilt among the ranks—how dare I overmuch boast and swagger, thereby adding to the burden of fault!"
proposals.after: I failed to strike the right balance in pacifying and defending the people, and so encouraged the rebels. I ought now to take the blame, reproach myself and acknowledge my guilt before the ranks. How dare I boast extravagantly and make my fault still greater?”
proposals.reason: The sentence connects failures of pacification and defense to the rise of rebellion and adds 歸罪行間 after Hong takes personal responsibility. Preserve the military setting without shifting the blame onto his subordinates.

units.zh: 其右僕射韋華聞而謂河南太守慕容築曰：「皇太子實有恭惠之德，社稷之福也。」
units.en: Wei Hua told Murong Zhu: "The crown prince's humility is the dynasty's luck."
units.literal: His right vice-director Wei Hua heard it and said to Henan Grand Administrator Murong Zhu, "The crown prince truly has the virtue of reverence and kindness—blessing for the altars."

proposals.before: Wei Hua told Murong Zhu: "The crown prince's humility is the dynasty's luck."
proposals.after: Hearing of this, Wei Hua, the right vice-director, told Murong Zhu, governor of Henan, “The crown prince truly is respectful and kind. That is a blessing for the state.”
proposals.reason: Both offices, Hua hearing the incident, and 惠 as kindness in addition to respectful humility are explicit.

value.assessment: the crown prince has the virtue of reverence and kindness, a blessing for the altars

units.zh: 其弟弼有奪嫡之謀，泓恩撫如初，未嘗見於色。
units.en: His brother Yao Bi plotted to supplant him, yet Yao Hong treated him with unchanged kindness and never showed resentment.
units.literal: His younger brother Bi had a plan to seize the heirship; Hong treated him with favor as at first and never showed it in his expression.

proposals.before: His brother Yao Bi plotted to supplant him, yet Yao Hong treated him with unchanged kindness and never showed resentment.
proposals.after: His younger brother Yao Bi plotted to supplant him, yet Yao Hong treated him with unchanged kindness and never showed resentment.
proposals.reason: 弟 specifies a younger brother.

value.action: plotted to seize the heirship from p001
continued to treat p015 with unchanged favor without showing resentment

units.zh: 姚紹每為弼羽翼，泓亦推心宗事，弗以為嫌。
units.en: Yao Shao backed Yao Bi, but Yao Hong still trusted him as kin and showed no distrust.
units.literal: Yao Shao often acted as wings for Bi; Hong also gave him whole-hearted clan duty and did not take it as suspicion.

proposals.before: Yao Shao backed Yao Bi, but Yao Hong still trusted him as kin and showed no distrust.
proposals.after: Yao Shao repeatedly supported Bi, yet Hong trusted and honored Shao wholeheartedly and bore him no suspicion on that account.
proposals.reason: 宗事 entails deference or honoring Shao; 嫌 means Hong harbored no suspicion against him on this account.

proposals.before: Yao Shao often acted as wings for Bi; Hong also gave him whole-hearted clan duty and did not take it as suspicion.
proposals.after: Yao Shao repeatedly supported Bi, yet Hong trusted and honored Shao wholeheartedly and bore him no suspicion on that account.
proposals.reason: 宗事 entails deference or honoring Shao; 嫌 means Hong harbored no suspicion against him on this account.

units.zh: 及僭立，任紹以兵權，紹亦感而歸誠，卒守其忠烈。
units.en: Once Yao Hong took the throne he gave Yao Shao real command; Shao repaid him with loyalty unto death.
units.literal: When he presumptuously mounted the throne, he entrusted Shao with military authority; Shao was also moved and returned sincerity, and in the end kept his loyal fierceness.

proposals.before: Once Yao Hong took the throne he gave Yao Shao real command; Shao repaid him with loyalty unto death.
proposals.after: When Yao Hong claimed the imperial throne, he entrusted Yao Shao with military command. Moved by this, Shao pledged himself to Hong and remained loyal to the end.
proposals.reason: 僭 conveys the narrator’s view of Hong’s imperial claim, and 感 gives Shao’s response to Hong’s trust.

value.action: presumptuously took the throne and entrusted p016 with military authority

value.assessment: kept loyal fierceness to the end

units.zh: 其明識寬裕，皆此類也。
units.en: His judgment and magnanimity ran in that vein throughout.
units.literal: His clear insight and generous breadth were all of this sort.

units.zh: 興既死，秘不發喪。
units.en: When Yao Xing died, the court hid the news.
units.literal: After Xing died, they secretly did not issue mourning.

value.action: kept Xing's death secret then later issued mourning

units.zh: 南陽公姚愔及大將軍尹元等謀為亂，泓皆誅之。
units.en: Yao Yin, Yin Yuan, and their fellow plotters were put to death.
units.literal: Duke of Nanyang Yao Yin and Grand General Yin Yuan and others plotted rebellion; Hong executed them all.

proposals.before: Yao Yin, Yin Yuan, and their fellow plotters were put to death.
proposals.after: Yao Yin, Duke of Nanyang, Grand General Yin Yuan and others plotted rebellion. Yao Hong put them all to death.
proposals.reason: Restore both offices, the plot to rebel and Hong as the executor.

value.action: plotted rebellion with p018 and others

units.zh: 命其齊公姚恢殺安定太守呂超，恢久乃誅之。
units.en: He told Duke Qi Yao Hui to kill Lü Chao, governor of Anding; Yao Hui dragged his feet before obeying.
units.literal: He ordered Duke of Qi Yao Hui to kill Anding Grand Administrator Lü Chao; Hui long delayed before killing him.

units.zh: 泓疑恢有陰謀，恢自是懷貳，陰聚兵甲焉。
units.en: Yao Hong suspected treason; Yao Hui began to hedge and stockpile arms in secret.
units.literal: Hong suspected Hui had a hidden plot; Hui from this harbored two minds and secretly gathered armor and weapons.

value.action: suspected p019 of a hidden plot
harbored divided loyalty and secretly gathered arms

units.zh: 泓發喪，以義熙十二年僭即帝位，大赦殊死已下，改元永和，廬於諮議堂。
units.en: Yao Hong announced the death, and in the twelfth year of Yixi claimed the throne, declared a general amnesty short of capital crimes, adopted the era Yonghe, and mourned in a hut beside the council hall.
units.literal: Hong issued mourning; in the twelfth year of Yixi he presumptuously assumed the imperial seat, greatly pardoned all short of capital crime, changed the era to Yonghe, and lodged in a mourning hut at the consultation hall.

proposals.before: Yao Hong announced the death, and in the twelfth year of Yixi claimed the throne, declared a general amnesty short of capital crimes, adopted the era Yonghe, and mourned in a hut beside the council hall.
proposals.after: Yao Hong announced the mourning. In the twelfth year of Yixi he claimed the imperial throne, issued a general pardon extending even to those condemned to death, changed the era name to Yonghe and took up quarters in a mourning hut at the council hall.
proposals.reason: 殊死已下 includes prisoners sentenced to death and those with lesser sentences. Both fields reverse that scope.

proposals.before: Hong issued mourning; in the twelfth year of Yixi he presumptuously assumed the imperial seat, greatly pardoned all short of capital crime, changed the era to Yonghe, and lodged in a mourning hut at the consultation hall.
proposals.after: Yao Hong announced the mourning. In the twelfth year of Yixi he claimed the imperial throne, issued a general pardon extending even to those condemned to death, changed the era name to Yonghe and took up quarters in a mourning hut at the council hall.
proposals.reason: 殊死已下 includes prisoners sentenced to death and those with lesser sentences. Both fields reverse that scope.

value.action: kept Xing's death secret then later issued mourning

value.note: presumptuously assumed the imperial seat; changed era to Yonghe

label.en: general amnesty short of capital crimes

value.action: lodged in a mourning hut at the consultation hall

units.zh: 既葬，乃親庶政，內外百僚增位一等，令文武各盡直言，政有不便於時，事有光益宗廟者，極言勿有所諱。
units.en: After the funeral he took the reins himself, promoted every official a grade, and invited blunt counsel on what helped or hurt the state.
units.literal: After burial, he then personally attended to myriad government; inner and outer hundred officials were raised one rank in position; he ordered civil and military each to exhaust straight speech—where government had what was not convenient to the time, or affairs that could add lustre to the ancestral temple, speak to the utmost without hiding.

proposals.before: After the funeral he took the reins himself, promoted every official a grade, and invited blunt counsel on what helped or hurt the state.
proposals.after: After the burial Hong took charge of government himself and promoted every official at court and in the provinces by one rank. He ordered civil and military officers alike to speak freely about policies unsuited to the times and measures that would bring honor and benefit to the dynasty, holding nothing back.
proposals.reason: Restore civil and military officials, the policy question, benefit to the ancestral dynasty and injunction to speak without reserve.

value.action: after burial took personal charge, promoted inner and outer officials one rank, invited blunt counsel

units.zh: 初，興徙李閏羌三千家于安定，尋徙新支。
units.en: Yao Xing had earlier moved three thousand Li-run Qiang households to Anding, then shifted them again to Xin-zhi.
units.literal: At first, Xing had moved three thousand households of Li-run Qiang to Anding, then soon moved them to Xin-zhi.

value.action: moved three thousand Li-run Qiang households to Anding then to Xin-zhi

units.zh: 至是，羌酋党容率所部叛還，遣撫軍姚贊討之。
units.en: Their chief Dang Rong then bolted for home; Yao Hong sent Yao Zan against him.
units.literal: At this point, Qiang chief Dang Rong led his following in revolt to return; he sent General Who Pacifies Yao Zan to campaign against him.

proposals.before: Their chief Dang Rong then bolted for home; Yao Hong sent Yao Zan against him.
proposals.after: The Qiang chief Dang Rong then led his followers in revolt and set out for home. Yao Hong sent Pacifying General Yao Zan to attack him.
proposals.reason: The chief leads his following in revolt, and Yao Zan bears the Pacifying Army title.

value.action: led followers in revolt to return
sent p022 to campaign against p021

units.zh: 容降，徙其豪右數百戶于長安，余遣還李閏。
units.en: Dang Rong yielded; Yao Hong moved the head families to Chang'an and let the rest go home to Li-run.
units.literal: Rong surrendered; he moved several hundred notable households to Chang'an and sent the rest back to Li-run.

proposals.before: Dang Rong yielded; Yao Hong moved the head families to Chang'an and let the rest go home to Li-run.
proposals.after: Dang Rong surrendered. Yao Hong moved several hundred of the leading households to Chang’an and sent the rest back to Lirun.
proposals.reason: 數百戶 gives a specific approximate count.

value.action: moved several hundred notable households to Chang'an and sent the rest back to Li-run

units.zh: 北地太守毛雍據趙氏塢以叛于泓，姚紹討擒之。
units.en: Mao Yong of Beidi seized the Zhao stockade in revolt; Yao Shao captured him.
units.literal: Beidi Grand Administrator Mao Yong occupied the Zhao clan stockade and rebelled against Hong; Yao Shao campaigned, seized him.

proposals.before: Mao Yong of Beidi seized the Zhao stockade in revolt; Yao Shao captured him.
proposals.after: Mao Yong, governor of Beidi, occupied the Zhao clan’s stockade in revolt against Yao Hong. Yao Shao attacked and captured him.
proposals.reason: 太守 makes Mao governor of Beidi, and he revolted against Hong.

value.action: occupied the Zhao clan stockade and rebelled against p001

units.zh: 姚宣時鎮李閏，未知雍敗，遣部將姚佛生等來衛長安。
units.en: Yao Xuan was then garrisoning Lirun and had not yet learned that Mao Yong had been defeated, so he sent his subordinate commander Yao Fosheng and others to defend Chang'an.
units.literal: Yao Xuan then garrisoned Li-run, not yet knowing of Yong's defeat, sent subordinate generals Yao Fosheng and others to come guard Chang'an.

value.action: sent p025 and others to guard Chang'an, not yet knowing p023's defeat

units.zh: 眾既發，宣參軍韋宗奸諂好亂，說宣曰：「主上初立，威化末著，勃勃強盛，侵害必深，本朝之難未可弭也。
units.en: Adviser Wei Zong, a troublemaker, told Yao Xuan: "The new ruler lacks prestige; Helian Bobo is too strong—the capital's troubles are not over.
units.literal: Once the host had set out, Xuan's adviser Wei Zong, fawning and fond of turmoil, spoke to Xuan, saying, "The lord has just risen, awe and transformation are not yet manifest; Bobo is strong and flourishing, harm and invasion will surely be deep; the hardship of this court is not yet to be stilled.

proposals.before: Adviser Wei Zong, a troublemaker, told Yao Xuan: "The new ruler lacks prestige; Helian Bobo is too strong—the capital's troubles are not over.
proposals.after: After the troops had set out, Yao Xuan’s adviser Wei Zong, a deceitful flatterer who delighted in disorder, urged him, “The ruler has only just taken the throne, and his authority is not yet established. Helian Bobo is powerful, and his incursions are sure to cause great harm. Our court’s troubles cannot yet be put to rest.
proposals.reason: Restore the troops’ departure, Zong’s deceit and flattery, the predicted invasive harm and the threat to the court.

value.action: described as strong and certain to invade deeply

units.zh: 殿下居維城之任，宜深慮之。
units.en: You hold the western shield—think hard.
units.literal: Your Highness holds the duty of the bulwark city—you ought deeply to ponder it.

proposals.before: You hold the western shield—think hard.
proposals.after: Your Highness has the duty of protecting the ruling house. You should consider this carefully.
proposals.reason: 維城 depicts the prince’s duty as a bulwark of the state, without a western direction.

units.zh: 邢望地形險固，總三方之要，若能據之，虛心撫禦，非但克固維城，亦霸王之業也。」
units.en: Xingwang is a natural fortress commanding three approaches—seize it in earnest and you secure the west and maybe build a power base."
units.literal: Xingwang's terrain is perilous and firm, gathering the key of three directions—if you can occupy it, with empty mind soothe and control, not only can you solidify the bulwark, it is also the enterprise of a hegemon-king."

proposals.before: Xingwang is a natural fortress commanding three approaches—seize it in earnest and you secure the west and maybe build a power base."
proposals.after: Xingwang is naturally defensible and commands the approaches from three directions. If you occupy it and govern the people there with an open mind, you can secure your position as a bulwark of the dynasty and even lay the foundations of a hegemon’s or a king’s rule.”
proposals.reason: Recover willing and open-minded governance, the dynastic bulwark and the prospect of hegemonic or royal power.

units.zh: 宣乃率戶三萬八千，棄李閏，南保邢望。
units.en: Yao Xuan marched thirty-eight thousand households south from Li-run to fortify Xingwang.
units.literal: Xuan then led thirty-eight thousand households, abandoned Li-run, and went south to hold Xingwang.

proposals.before: Yao Xuan marched thirty-eight thousand households south from Li-run to fortify Xingwang.
proposals.after: Yao Xuan abandoned Lirun and led thirty-eight thousand households south to hold Xingwang.
proposals.reason: 棄李閏 is abandonment of the garrison; 保 is holding the refuge at Xingwang.

value.action: led 38000 households, abandoned Li-run, went south to hold Xingwang

units.zh: 宣既南移，諸羌據李閏以叛，紹進討破之。
units.en: When Yao Xuan left, the Qiang seized Li-run; Yao Shao smashed them.
units.literal: Once Xuan had moved south, the various Qiang occupied Li-run in revolt; Shao advanced and campaigned, defeated them.

proposals.before: When Yao Xuan left, the Qiang seized Li-run; Yao Shao smashed them.
proposals.after: Once Yao Xuan had moved south, the Qiang groups occupied Lirun in revolt. Yao Shao advanced against them and defeated them.
proposals.reason: 以叛 is an explicit revolt.

value.action: advanced, campaigned, and defeated Qiang who occupied Li-run after p024 left

units.zh: 宣詣紹歸罪，紹怒殺之。
units.en: Yao Xuan surrendered to Yao Shao, who killed him in fury.
units.literal: Xuan went to Shao to confess guilt; Shao in anger killed him.

proposals.before: Yao Xuan surrendered to Yao Shao, who killed him in fury.
proposals.after: Yao Xuan went to Yao Shao to acknowledge his guilt. Shao killed him in anger.
proposals.reason: 歸罪 identifies Xuan’s acknowledgment of fault.

value.action: went to p016 to confess guilt

units.zh: 初，宣在邢望，泓遣姚佛生諭宣，佛生遂贊成宣計。
units.en: Earlier Yao Hong had sent Yao Fosheng to recall Yao Xuan; Fosheng instead backed the defection.
units.literal: At first, while Xuan was at Xingwang, Hong sent Yao Fosheng to instruct Xuan; Fosheng then endorsed Xuan's plan.

proposals.before: Earlier Yao Hong had sent Yao Fosheng to recall Yao Xuan; Fosheng instead backed the defection.
proposals.after: Earlier, when Yao Xuan was at Xingwang, Yao Hong had sent Yao Fosheng to reason with him. Fosheng ended up supporting Xuan’s plan.
proposals.reason: Restore the location and avoid supplying a specific recall order or calling Xuan’s plan a defection.

value.action: sent p025 to instruct p024 at Xingwang
endorsed p024's plan instead of recalling him

units.zh: 紹數其罪，又戮之。
units.en: Yao Shao listed Fosheng's crimes and put him to death too.
units.literal: Shao enumerated his crimes and executed him as well.

units.zh: 泓下書，士卒死王事，贈以爵位，永復其家。
units.en: He decreed pensions and perpetual exemptions for families of soldiers who died in royal service.
units.literal: Hong issued a document: soldiers who died in the king's service were granted rank and title, and their families were forever exempted.

proposals.before: He decreed pensions and perpetual exemptions for families of soldiers who died in royal service.
proposals.after: Yao Hong decreed that soldiers who died in royal service should receive posthumous titles and their families should enjoy perpetual exemption from levies.
proposals.reason: 贈以爵位 is the posthumous award of titles, not a pension for surviving relatives.

value.action: granted rank to soldiers who died in royal service and perpetual household exemption

units.zh: 將封宮臣十六人五等子男，姚贊諫曰：「東宮文武，自當有守忠之誠，未有赫然之效，何受封之多乎？」
units.en: Yao Zan objected to raising sixteen household officers to noble rank: "The heir's staff owes loyalty by duty—they have done nothing spectacular yet."
units.literal: He was about to enfeoff sixteen palace officials as fifth-rank barons and viscounts; Yao Zan remonstrated, saying, "Eastern-palace civil and military naturally ought to have the loyalty of guarding unto death—they have not yet had blazing manifest merit; how can they receive so many enfeoffments?"

proposals.before: Yao Zan objected to raising sixteen household officers to noble rank: "The heir's staff owes loyalty by duty—they have done nothing spectacular yet."
proposals.after: Hong proposed making sixteen palace officers viscounts or barons. Yao Zan objected, “Surely the crown prince’s civil and military officers owe him loyalty as a matter of duty. They have shown no conspicuous merit. Why grant them so many fiefs?”
proposals.reason: Restore Hong’s intention, the two noble ranks, the civil and military staff, and Zan’s question about the extensive grants.

proposals.before: He was about to enfeoff sixteen palace officials as fifth-rank barons and viscounts; Yao Zan remonstrated, saying, "Eastern-palace civil and military naturally ought to have the loyalty of guarding unto death—they have not yet had blazing manifest merit; how can they receive so many enfeoffments?"
proposals.after: He was about to enfeoff sixteen palace officials as viscounts and barons in the five grades of nobility. Yao Zan remonstrated, “The Eastern Palace’s civil and military officers naturally owe it faithful loyalty. They have yet to show conspicuous merit. Why should they receive so many grants of fiefs?”
proposals.reason: 五等 is the five-grade system, not an ordinal shared by the fourth and fifth grades; 守忠 does not specify death.

value.action: was about to enfeoff sixteen palace officials as fifth-rank viscounts and barons, then desisted
